correctness.rationale: Definitions of spanned lines and planes are exact for all subsets including empty sets. The incidence classification yields explicit f1 and f2 formulas. The standalone checker independently reconstructs 58 line and 43 plane flats by determinants over Q(zeta), enumerates all 2^12=4096 subsets with both methods, asserts equality for every case and exactly five negative subsets, and checks 12 deletions. The four proper negative subsets lie on coordinate-face planes; full S has rank four. The exhaustive finite algorithm proves a finite classification, with no inference to other arrangements.

originality.rationale: The classification of negative-defect restrictions of the fixed twelve-point set and the essential deletion-minimality conclusion have different quantifiers and implications from the known full-configuration flat counts and full-m-family threshold. Two highly relevant complete primary texts were inspected. Five targeted semantic research-record queries and general web queries did not locate equivalent coverage. This is qualified rather than absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: Deleting hyperplanes is the natural local test of whether a newly published counterexample is a primitive obstruction to the proposed Purdy inequality. The complete restriction theorem distinguishes exactly four nonessential planar artifacts from the unique essential negative subset, supplies a sharp deletion stability statement (all twelve deletions have defect six), and is not recoverable from the known total f-vector alone. This is a motivated exact classification of a finite natural incidence structure; no claim of general universality is made.
